method: Interview themes used for discovery priorities; all published additions below are supported by public operator or program pages. No private interview statements are included.

MARS Unmanned Aircraft Systems Airfield.test_aircraft: Government and commercial UAS; multi-domain testing, training, demonstrations, and exercises.
MARS Unmanned Aircraft Systems Airfield.test_dimensions: 3,000 x 75 ft runway; vertical takeoff and landing pad; 90 x 50 ft hangar. Direct access to 75 square nautical miles of restricted airspace.
MARS Unmanned Aircraft Systems Airfield.test_access: Secure federal facility. Coordinate mission integration and airfield access with the Virginia Spaceport Authority; published dimensions do not establish aircraft-specific approval.

Virginia Tech Drone Park.test_aircraft: Drone research, education, and technology testing inside a netted enclosure.
Virginia Tech Drone Park.test_dimensions: 300 x 120 x 85 ft netted enclosure, approximately three million cubic feet of flight space; adjacent laboratory and classroom space. This is not an open-air runway.
Virginia Tech Drone Park.test_access: Request flight time through VTDronePark@vt.edu, review the park protocol, and complete the orientation. Commercial and third-party operations have additional requirements.

NASA Langley UAS Test Range.test_aircraft: Small research UAS. The cited July 2015 opening announcement describes the initial operating scope, not current aircraft approvals.
NASA Langley UAS Test Range.test_dimensions: 100-acre range reported in the 2015 opening announcement. Current launch-area and runway dimensions are not established by that source.
NASA Langley UAS Test Range.test_access: NASA's opening announcement requires scheduling through the UAS Operations Office, airspace coordination, security notification, and a range safety officer. Confirm current conditions with NASA; the historical limits are not a present-day authorization.

NASA Langley Research Center.current_activity: Langley's public Front Door brings together research facilities, capabilities, technology transfer, small-business programs, and partnerships information.
NASA Langley Research Center.partnership_opportunities: Prospective industry, academic, and other partners can use the Front Door's Connecting with Langley route to submit a statement of interest to the partnerships team.

records.name: Commonwealth STEM Industry Internship Program (CSIIP)
records.short_description: Virginia Space Grant Consortium program connecting employers and undergraduates with paid STEM internships.
records.overview: CSIIP is a statewide workforce program coordinated by Hampton-based VSGC, rather than a single training or flight site. Employers register and hire interns directly; the program provides student matching and staff support. The regional classification identifies the coordinator, not the program's service boundary.
records.unmanned_systems_relevance: Supporting workforce resource for UxS employers recruiting engineering, computer science, cybersecurity, and data-science talent. The program explicitly includes aviation and UAV internships.
records.contact_text: Sarah Pauls, CSIIP public program contact
records.current_activity: The public program page lists ongoing registration for students and employers.
records.partnership_opportunities: Employers can register internships through the company route; students use the separate student registration route. Confirm current eligibility and support with the program.

records.name: STEM Takes Flight at Virginia's Community Colleges
records.short_description: VSGC, VCCS, and NASA research-experience program for Virginia community college STEM students and faculty.
records.overview: The initiative connects community college students with paid research experiences at NASA Langley and Wallops and offers faculty professional development. It is coordinated by Hampton-based VSGC and serves participants across Virginia rather than a single mapped training site. The regional classification identifies the coordinator, not the program's service boundary.
records.unmanned_systems_relevance: Supporting aerospace and technical workforce pathway, including community college technician tracks. Participation does not itself establish drone-pilot certification or UAS-specific project placement.
records.contact_text: Nicole Shaw, student research experience contact
records.current_activity: The published 2026 student research session ran June 1-August 7. Those application deadlines have passed; a later intake has not been confirmed in this record.
records.partnership_opportunities: Students and faculty should consult the program's separate information and application routes and ask about the next announced cycle.
